title: Farewell to the Past
subtitle: Clasp your hands, bow your head, and become a figure gazed upon.

items.text: When the voice of this outsider fades, the fated hour also arrives. Those among the crowd who drank the liquor undergo a transformation amidst chaotic screams, as each and every one of them becomes a Lùshǔ.
As Jiǔ Niángzǐ watches this irreversible scene, she is unaware that tears are already flowing down her face.
She has made no progress at all. Everything is no different now than it was a few years ago, when she was even more reckless and naive.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: The Daoist told me that my mother was the ninth Lùshǔ from the very beginning of time.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Great, though, distant.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: After all, except for the moment she turned from a human into a Yāo when she was leaving ...

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: I don't quite remember her.

items.speaker: Daoist
items.text: Your mother was the Xiángruì, the people's guardian.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi (Child)
items.text: What is a Xiángruì?

items.speaker: Daoist
items.text: The spirit of auspiciousness, the great Yāo who protects and benefits people, like your mother once did.

items.speaker: Daoist
items.text: But a Xiángruì is not supposed to have any personal feelings. She fell because of you, because of the personal feeling. Remember that.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi (Child)
items.text: What is a "personal feeling"?

items.speaker: Daoist
items.text: It's something she shouldn't have had, for you, either.

items.speaker: Daoist
items.text: But you shall keep to the path she left.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi (Child)
items.text: What path?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi (Child)
items.text: Is it like the dirt path we're walking on, or, or the stone path around the house?

items.speaker: Daoist
items.text: Neither.

items.speaker: Daoist
items.text: Stay in this city. Be their guardian. Be a Xiángruì.

items.speaker: Daoist
items.text: You shall understand when the day comes.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: The Daoist brought me here, and left me here.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: That's exactly what my mother, the former Xiángruì, did to me as well. So I took departure as the price of living in the human world.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Before I came into Pèi City, the Daoist guaranteed me that ...

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: "Be a Xiángruì, and then you will understand her."

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: How alluring was that! That's why I chose to stay here.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: At first, I couldn't stop thinking about what the Daoist said, but I had no idea how.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Because I was never taught how by anyone.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: I didn't have any other choice, so ...

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: So I started to recall my mother by piecing together the scattered words and descriptions from books and legends, to recall what a Xiángruì is.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: I tried to be her, tried to replace her.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Just to meet her, once again.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: If I got to meet her, I would ask her, "What was on your mind?"

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: If only you could see me doing such a great job as a Xiángruì, would you feel even the slightest twinge of guilt? For deserting me, for leaving me alone.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Well.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Looks like I've neither truly understood her, nor a Xiángruì.
Between the two people standing in the courtyard walkway in the silent rain, a decision is made.

items.speaker: Facao
items.text: Jiǔ Niángzǐ, are you really going to ...

As someone who has always been steadfast in his will, he rarely hesitates. He doesn't know which words to use to emphasize the danger of this matter to the person in front of him, or whether all words are powerless before her final choice.
And so, ultimately, he remains silent.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: It's fine. I know there's no one who could jump over it. In order to stop me, Lǐzhèng even told me some stories, and they were ... not very suitable for children.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: But I have to, because there is no other way ...

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Only The Divination.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Well, you can't talk about Shuòrì without The Divination, right?

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Thank you for letting me go. You even brought me the clothes. But the Zhílǐ is not here. I'm not sure if I'm wearing it right ...

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: But it's ok. Even if it's wrong, it still looks new and colorful.

She pats the hem of her skirt aimlessly, then folds the cuffs, and finally folds back the silk drapes once more. When she cannot find anything else to fix, her farewell rises to the tip of her tongue.

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: Thank you. Thank you so very much. I-er, I ...

items.speaker: Jiu Niangzi
items.text: I'm leaving, then.
Jiǔ Niángzǐ steps back and places her hands beneath her forehead, palm to back. She bows farewell to Fǎcáo in the hallway and the Lùshǔ turned from Lǐzhèng.
A gesture of gratitude and an apology. She has never performed such a ritual before—this will be the first and last time.

items.speaker: Facao
items.text: Perhaps we will find another way. You don't have to ...
He doesn't finish. Because anything he wants to say would be untrue, an example of unwarranted comfort from a survivor toward their aggressor.
And so, Jiǔ Niángzǐ says nothing. She shakes her head as if she hadn't even heard his proposal, retreating into the rain, and then turns around and walks towards the outside of the Zhící.
Her footsteps have never been so relaxed before, with each step becoming faster and faster, almost evolving into a sprint toward the end.
She runs toward the outside of the city, but not to escape.
Broken Bridge, Outside the City
The rain has not stopped since the previous night.
Outside the city, Bessmert and Yenisei stand at the end of the broken bridge, gazing at the misty bank opposite to them.
Gětiān is perched on the tree above their heads. He has been here all along, arriving earlier than the others.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Mr. Gětiān, we ...

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: We are left with only one option, which is to stand here and pray for her, correct?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Pray that the Ask and Acquire, or The Divination, will answer us and give us what we want in a flash.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: But is it really possible?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: I think not. We should go.
Bessmert listens to the advancing footsteps around her, emanating from all those who are walking toward the broken bridge, still remembering the auspicious significance of this New Year's Day.
At first, she tries to distinguish the voices that might be Fǎcáo and the others, but as the rain grows heavier and louder, she finally gives up.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I heard today is a special day for the locals, known as "Suìzhāochūn."

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Mr. Gětiān, what is Suìzhāochūn?
Bessmert holds her wet fringe to one side, and tilts the oiled umbrella towards Yenisei.
The Lùshǔ silently approaches and leans against her tightly.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: It comes from an ancient proverb, "Bǎizǎi Nánféng Suìzhāochūn."

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: It's the first day of a new year and the first day of spring.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Lìchūn, the beginning of spring, corresponds to the lower trigram of Kǎn in the direction of Gèn. It is the season of life.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: A time when the weather is clear and Yáng fills the air.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: They are pleasing to the ears.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: But I don't know what to make of it when all these are put together.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Lìchūn is one of the 24 solar terms. It signifies the beginning of spring.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Suìzhāochūn is how people would call it when the first day of the Dùshuò Festival and the first day of spring happen to be the same day. It is a once-in-a-century good sign.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Indeed. It's also the first day of a new year. I like the coincidence.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Do you still find it equally pleasing if your teammates are not coming back?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Then, I will take them home as they are now and see what I can do.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I know the words are hidden behind your silence, but this is the best option for now.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: After all, as you just said, prayers are not enough to bring them back.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: They could, for a time.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: But that's only what happened in the past, as you just said. Good days only exist in our memories.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: That was before the flood. The aftermath of that disaster lasted longer than I thought.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: I was so wrong to think it was over.
Bessmert looks up. A drop of rain falls right onto the fabric she uses to cover her eyes. Then more falls, and more, gradually wetting the entire weaved surface.
She listens without intending any comment.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: It all began with the unstoppable flood. At first, it was just a few unusual tides that no one noticed.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Then the flood came, followed by the destruction of the bridge.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: The temple on the mountain thus lost its connection to its pilgrims. The prayers were no longer answered.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: I do not understand what caused all these things. My people left the mountain to help with the situation, but they never came back.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: And now ...

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Even this river beneath us is gone, just like the Yuān Temple, forever lost in the fog.
Behind them, the city residents gradually approach and carve words of divination onto the wooden sticks in their hands, just as they had in previous years.
They are prepared for the fact that there may not be an answer to their questions, but they know nothing of the reason why.
Bessmert feels the weight of the growing crowd. They gather and write in the rain, working tirelessly for a long time.
Is it the eternal fate of humans and arcanists to act upon desires they know cannot be realized?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: It's useless. The god won't hear us, nor will It see us.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Please know that I don't mean to offend you with this question.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Please.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Can't you take those people to the other end of the bridge?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: If the condition of The Divination is to go across the broken bridge ...

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Though we are both outsiders in this place, you're more naive than I am.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Emm ...?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: One can only meet the condition by going over the bridge oneself, even if the price is their life.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: You might think it's cruel. But what good would it do if people were easily given what they asked for without paying a price?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Wouldn't it make others' suffering a joke?
Gětiān lowers his head to look at Bessmert and the quiet Yenisei beside him, thinking that they perhaps do not believe his words.
He rarely needs to say so much to others in such a short space of time. But since he has already started, he might as well finish.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: You don't believe me.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I'm ... trying to understand.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: It's all the same. I can take you to the other side of the bridge, but you must not be disappointed if it ends up fruitless.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Pardon?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: I can take you there.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Why? Why the change of mind?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Mm? Haven't I mentioned it before?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Mentioned what?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Your bones. Among all the others, you are the only one for whom I do not recognize the markings on your bones.
